source.title: Language Models Can Explain Visual Features via Steering
source.authors: Javier Ferrando; Enrique Lopez-Cuena; P. A. Martin-Torres; Daniel Hinjos; Anna Arias-Duart; D. García-Gasulla

record.tranche_reason: The study compares explanation-quality metrics across language-model sizes, a different measure and task from the pretraining-loss scaling claim. It tests the downstream-performance version only.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit loss-scaling laws, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its reported explanation-quality comparisons across Gemma 3 explainer sizes bear on V6. Comparisons among Steering, Top-k, and hybrid explanation methods are not rows for the scaling claim.
record.test_reason: An interpretability paper whose only scale result is a side experiment. It varies the Gemma 3 explainer LM size (4B, 12B, 27B) with the vision encoder and SAE fixed, and reports that explanation-quality metrics improve with size. This is a directional result on V6 in a new downstream setting (automated explanation of vision SAE features). It is not the same method as the originals and not a dedicated alternative test, so T3 rather than T2. It says nothing about loss, extrapolation, allocation, shape or fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: explanation quality of Steering scales consistently with LM size, and the hybrid Steering-informed Top-k gives the best explanations across metrics. The authors also state that Steering alone generally underperforms Top-k.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies explainer-model size and measures visual-feature explanation quality; it does not use the original sources' pretraining-loss sweeps or compute-optimal allocation fits.
record.method_sensitivity: The scale trend is reported for Gemma 3 Steering explanations on a middle-layer vision-encoder SAE; the tested explainer sizes are 4B, 12B, and 27B.
record.problems: The size comparison tests only three explainer sizes and reports plotted values without exact numbers or uncertainty for the scale trend. It does not fit or test a predictive scaling relationship.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: Whether the improvement is predictable: no fit, no extrapolation and no relation to pretraining loss. Only one task and one model family. No other downstream tasks.
All: no fitted laws or extrapolation.
All: no shape variation at fixed parameters.
All: no loss power laws in other modalities or regimes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label was removed: 'not a fitted prediction' is an untested part, not a qualifying result. Possible confound: with a blank image and no steering, Gemma 3 27B hallucinates a bird while 4B and 12B correctly describe a blank image (Appendix G.2). So the larger model's behaviour differs in ways other than explanation quality. Only three points, all from one model family, so this is weak evidence for V6.

relationships.condition: Steering explanations of a middle-layer SAE on the Gemma 3 SigLIP encoder, with Gemma 3 4B/12B/27B as explainer
relationships.reason: Synthetic activation and AUROC rise monotonically from 4B to 12B to 27B (r1, r2). IoU and CLIP are reported as a positive trend (r3, r4), but the figure caption is inconsistent. This is direction only, not a quantitative prediction.
relationships.display_finding: Synthetic activation and AUROC increased monotonically from 4B to 12B to 27B; IoU and CLIP trends were reported positive despite an inconsistent caption, without quantitative forecasts.
